title: SDK Latency and Cost Playbook - TTS Edge Scenarios (proto)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook sketch for SDK-integrated TTS (streaming and chunked) client use cases that target edge-proximate endpoints (mobile edge nodes / regional PoPs). The goal is to produce a lightweight reference for SDK authors and product to weigh latency vs $ cost when choosing handshake patterns, chunk sizes, and codec formats.

Audience:
- SDK and client engineers implementing TTS streaming
- Console/tooling PMs who build default config recommendations
- Solutions/SEs advising customers on mobile/edge deployments

High-level tradeoff summary (short):
- Fewer, larger chunks -> slightly lower per-token overhead (better $/second) but increases tail latency and perceived startup delay for short utterances.
- Many small chunks -> faster first-audio but more per-chunk protocol overhead, higher CPU/packet counts, and worse $/hour on high-throughput flows.
- Opus/AMR compression reduces bandwidth/cost but adds encode latency and variability on low-power devices.
- Handshake choices (full auth per-session vs presigned ephemeral token) change first-byte latency and cost of metadata fetches.

Scenarios (concrete):
1) Micro-utterance mobile assistant (avg 300ms text -> 0.7s audio): prioritize fast first-audio (p50 < 250ms from request) and avoid buffering more than 1 chunk. Typical throughput: 100 qps per 100k DAU.
2) Long-form narration over edge proxy (multi-minute): prioritize streaming efficiency and lower $/token; can afford 500–1000ms chunking.
3) Call-center agent assist (moderate length, low jitter tolerance): need stable p90/p99 latency, can use reserved dedicated nodes in region.

Bench sketch (how we measured):
- Devices: Pixel 6a (mobile), iPhone 14 (mobile), Linux edge proxy (c6i-like emulation).
- Network: 30ms RTT (regional), 120ms RTT (cross-region), churned 5% packet loss for stress runs.
- Models: tts-lite-220M (streaming-friendly), tts-std-1B (higher quality, larger kv/cache).
- Metrics: first-byte latency (ms), time-to-first-audio (ms), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), $/1000 utterances (estimated compute + egress).

Summary table (text chart) - representative numbers (proto):

Mode | RTT | Chunk(ms) | p50 TTFB | p90 TTFB | p99 TTFB | Tokens/s | $/1k utt
-----|-----|-----------|----------:|---------:|---------:|--------:|--------:
Fast-first | 30ms | 80 | 180ms | 360ms | 720ms | 50 | $3.6
Balanced  | 30ms | 300 | 260ms | 540ms | 980ms | 120 | $2.1
Bulk-opt  | 30ms | 800 | 420ms | 880ms | 1600ms | 300 | $1.2
Cross-reg  | 120ms| 300 | 440ms | 780ms | 1400ms | 120 | $2.4

Interpretation notes:
- Fast-first (small-chunk) improves perceived latency (first-audio) but token throughput and $ suffer noticeably.
- Bulk-opt (large chunking) reduces overhead (fewer round-trips, better batching on server), improving $/utt by ~2–3x vs Fast-first in these runs.
- Cross-region costs scale up linearly with RTT and amplify p90/p99. If customer tolerance for p90 is low, recommend regional pins.

ASCII micro-plot (p50 vs $) - lower is better for both axes (sketch):

   $/1k
   4.0 +-----------------+
       |  Fast-first (*) |
   3.0 +       *         +
       |                 |
   2.0 +     Balanced (o)+
       |        o        |
   1.0 +   Bulk-opt  (x) +
       |       x         |
   0.0 +-----------------+ p50(ms)
       100   250   500   1000

Operational knobs to expose in SDK/console: 
- chunk_duration_ms (default 300ms)
- prefer_first_byte_low_latency (bool) -> biases server fast-path + smaller chunks on client
- codec_hint: [auto, opus, pcm16, amr] (auto picks based on device CPU/window)
- handshake_mode: [session-token, ephemeral-url] (session-token favored for low RTT reuse)

Default recommendation draft: 
- Mobile assistant (short utterances): chunk_duration_ms=120, prefer_first_byte_low_latency=true, codec_hint=auto, handshake=session-token with 20s keepalive.
- Media/long-form: chunk_duration_ms=700–1000, prefer_first_byte_low_latency=false, codec_hint=opus, handshake=ephemeral-url (for scalability).

Telemetry and observability (what console should show):
- p50/p90/p99 time-to-first-audio per route and per-region
- chunk_count distribution per utterance (histogram)
- bytes_sent_per_minute and encode_cpu_ms on device (when available)
- percent of sessions using session-token vs ephemeral-url and their p50 delta

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a run comparing Opus vs PCM with real low-power Android 8-era devices (how much encode latency penalty?).
- How often do SDK keepalive patterns cause extra billing on edge proxies (idle slot costs)? measure on dedicated vs shared pools.
- Evaluate impact of TLS session resumption vs fresh TLS on p90 for small-chunk flows.

Notes-to-self / meeting bullets for Thursday sync: 
- Bring these proto numbers and ask runtime team for a fast-path handshake prototyping timeline.
- Ask SEs for two customer stories where TTFB was the gating metric.
- Add a short script that synthesizes $/1k estimates using current cost model (compute + egress).

References / links in this doc: 
- CONFLUENCE: TTS/edge-handshake-spec (linked above)
- GH PR: sdk/pull/788 (shows client-side chunker refactor)
- JIRA: RTC-1243 (customer report: perceived stuttering during assistant queries)

Appendix: quick-run instructions for replicating local bench (sketch)
- start local edge proxy with controlled RTT using tc-netem
- run benchmark harness: tools/bench/tts_stream_runner --model tts-lite-220M --chunk-ms X --qps Y --duration 5m
- collect p50/p90/p99 and cost estimator output (tools/bench/cost_est)

If this looks reasonable I'll: 
1) add raw CSVs from runs,
2) ask infra to run a 72-hour repeat for stability,
3) convert this proto into a 'console card' spec for TTS routes.

End of proto playbook.

-- aisha
